trust_decision.summary: ffuf's SimpleRunner.Execute decides how many (possibly decompressed) response bytes it pulls into memory, and the only bound is the compressed Content-Length header, so the answer is 'unbounded' whenever that header is absent, small, or stripped by the transport's transparent gzip decode.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'response decompression bomb', so an engineer looks first at the Content-Encoding gzip/br/deflate branches and the io.ReadAll that consumes the decoded stream.

fix_sites.entry_point: RunnerProvider.Execute as used by the ffuf CLI fuzzing run (main.go:272 -> pkg/ffuf/job.go:409); also reached by autocalibration (pkg/ffuf/autocalibration.go:92) and replay-proxy (pkg/ffuf/job.go:500) through the same method

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The -od / -audit-log raw response dump is optional logging/diagnostic output that never feeds resp.Data, so a solver can call it a neighbouring output feature rather than the response-body read the advisory describes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Compressed responses under the cap must still be fully decoded so -fs/-fw/-fl matchers and ContentWords/ContentLines see decompressed content, and a body mislabelled 'Content-Encoding: gzip' must still fall back to the raw bytes instead of erroring; an over-broad fix that caps compressed bytes, refuses on decoder error, or stops storing the body breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: Content-Encoding: gzip with a decodable gzip stream (manual gzip.NewReader branch) - fix.diff:29-32
Content-Encoding: gzip where gzip.NewReader fails (must fall back to the raw body, not error) - fix.diff:29-32
transport-transparently-decoded gzip where the transport strips Content-Encoding and Content-Length - fix.diff:50-53
chunked response with no Content-Length so the Atoi guard is skipped - fix.diff:50-53
compressed body whose Content-Length is the small compressed size and passes the 5 MiB header guard - fix.diff:50-53
body that decompresses to more than MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE (capped and marked Cancelled) - fix.diff:54-59
body that decompresses to at most MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE (unchanged, must not be cancelled) - fix.diff:174-194

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The raw response dump written when -od or -audit-log is set calls httputil.DumpResponse(httpresp, true), which reads the whole body into a bytes.Buffer unbounded, before the new LimitReader is reached; on the default path the transport has already transparently gunzipped, so this is an unbounded decompressed read of the same sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Output-directory and audit-log dumping is an optional diagnostic/recording feature, not the fetch path the report describes, and it does not populate resp.Data.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~27 lines above the patched read; reached through the separate -od/-audit-log output feature (main.go:130, main.go:132) whose result writer stores resp.Raw (pkg/output/stdout.go:358)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Route the -od/-audit-log raw response dump through the same bounded reader (dump at most MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE bytes) instead of httputil.DumpResponse's unbounded read.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer fixing the decompression bomb would naturally follow the response-dump path in the same function, since the audit log and -od feature also record the response; a follow-up commit adding a cap here is exactly what a second reviewer would file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A response-side counterpart to Dump(), materialising the response body for replay/reproduction (main.go:430-432 already uses Dump for requests).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ffuf already has a public Dump method used to reproduce a request; adding a matching response dump that reads resp.Body would repeat the same unbounded read without the runner's cap.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: NewResponse is the single place an ffuf.Response is built from an *http.Response, so a body-copying or streaming variant added here would re-read the (possibly decompressed) stream without going through Execute's LimitReader.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Response construction point is the obvious place for a maintainer to prefetch or re-materialise the body; the size check lives in the runner, not in this constructor, so the cap would not apply.

O9_family: CWE-409 decompression bomb / unbounded decompressed-response read (resource exhaustion)

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.17 module (go.mod:3); `go build ./...` / `go test ./...`; deps declared in go.mod:5-18 and go.sum, no vendor directory
O10_build.project_tests: No test files in pkg/runner at the pinned commit (only pkg/runner/simple.go and pkg/runner/runner.go); existing suites are in pkg/ffuf, pkg/filter, pkg/output and pkg/input, e.g. pkg/output/audit_test.go:10 and pkg/filter/size_test.go:10; the fix adds the new pkg/runner/simple_test.go (fix.diff:64-194), so it is not in the pinned tree.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the io.ReadAll at pkg/runner/simple.go:202 in io.LimitReader inside the gzip/br/deflate branches (or add a decompressed-size check next to the Content-Length guard), which leaves the -od/-audit-log httputil.DumpResponse read at pkg/runner/simple.go:175 unbounded.
